variants.protected:
Elena has put the office in order again today.

Every paper is arranged by date. The receipts are in a stack of their own, by date, no longer by amount. The ledger is open at the page you stopped on yesterday.

There is a freshly sharpened pencil on the corner of the desk.

When she comes in with the water you are looking through that stack of receipts.

She sets the water down and stands there a moment without going.

“Mr Kessler, yesterday —”

And there she stops.

You say that he finished checking the accounts and left.

“Yes.”

She holds the tray against her front, takes half a step back towards the door, and stops again.

“Thank you.”

Then she goes out, faster than she usually walks.

You do not ask her what for.
variants.exposed:
Nobody has put the office in order today.

The papers are as you left them yesterday and last night’s tea cup is still on the corner of the desk.

She came once in the morning to take away what needed washing. She did not come in. She stood in the doorway and reached her hand through.

You called out to her.

“Sir,” she said.

Then a very long silence.

“It is nothing,” you said.

She nodded and went.
variants.audit_tail:
While you are sorting, you find that the few pages Timothy looked at yesterday have been tabbed again.

The tabs are at exactly the places where he stopped.

You did not ask anybody to do that.
